name: Cab depot
text: Cabs asleep in racks two decks tall, doors open, cabins swung level. Cleaning robots work down the rows overnight, changing scrubber beds and topping up each cabin's heliox. At half past four the racks wake from the far end, and the cabs go out to the lobbies before anyone has called one.

name: Rebuild shop
text: A long workshop where cabs come apart. Cabins hang from hoists while fitters re-felt the walls, renew the seats and check the door seals. Every rebuild adds a stamped plate under the bench. The fitters keep a running argument about whose rivets are neatest, and nobody has ever won it.

name: Seal shop
text: Door seals for a whole Ring's cabs, made and fitted here. Every cab door seals against its berth door so the cab keeps its own air, and a seal that weeps lets heliox into the tubes. The test bench hisses all day, a high, thin note in this air.

name: Night freight bay
text: By day, an empty hall of numbered bays. From midnight it fills with carts from the Quaysides, each packed for one lobby: groceries for a Mill Hall, bolts of cloth for a mender, a single crate of tomatoes. Empty cabs pull in, take a cart and go, every few seconds.

name: Interchange
text: Where a core meets the tubes. Behind these walls cabs leave the shafts, turn onto a loop or a cross-line and join platoons on the move, thousands an hour each way. Out here there is a corridor, a door with the core's number on it, and a faint hum in the floor.

name: Bridge gallery
text: Loops run on one level and cross-lines on the other, so the tubes cross on bridges. This gallery runs beside one: a walkway, a row of inspection hatches and a crew of two checking bolts by hand lamp. Now and then the walkway trembles as a platoon goes over.

name: Gas post
text: A small room of meters, one for every tube on this stretch of the deck, each showing how much air has crept into the helium through the berth doors. Most read almost nothing. When one creeps up, the post flushes that tube overnight and chalks its number on the board.

name: Mask lockers
text: Rows of masks on hooks, each with its own bottle of heliox and a name tag. Nobody goes into the tubes without one, because pure helium has no oxygen in it at all. Crews check each other's straps at the door, out loud, every time, even after thirty years.

name: Gimbal shop
text: Cabins lifted out of their cabs wait here on trolleys while the two-axis gimbals they swing on are stripped and tested. A rig tilts an empty cabin to and fro all day, slowly, while a fitter listens to its bearings with a brass rod pressed to her ear.

name: Fairing shop
text: Cabs climb their shafts floor first, so their top and bottom fairings take every scuff. Here the scuffed ones are filled, smoothed and refitted. Shelves of fairings line the walls, each chalked with its cab's number, and the sanding dust is swept up and sent to the Yards.

name: Coil gallery
text: A narrow gallery beside a tube, lined with the guideway coils that drive every cab that passes. Inspectors walk it with a cart of meters, testing one coil every few metres. They never see the cabs, only hear them: a faint tick in the wall, a rising hiss, and gone.

name: Spare cab store
text: A hall of spare cabs, kept back for big days and failures: the Lattice holds one spare for every five in service. Most stand dusted and ready for months. On Booking Day, when the whole drum goes somewhere at once, the store empties within the hour and the crew sweep the floor.

name: Sign shop
text: Where the Lattice's signs are made: lobby boards, berth numbers, and the loop signs that post two limits, one for each direction. An apprentice letters the old ones by hand because the shop always has. Over the door, in faded paint, is what every child learns: spinward high, antispinward low.

name: Stall post
text: A small room with a desk, a screen and a pusher cab parked in a berth outside. If a cab stalls on this deck, the guideway's motors or the cab behind will nudge it to a berth; the pusher goes out only if they can't. The crew keep it polished anyway.

name: Crew hatch
text: A hatch in the wall, a kettle on the 65 °C tap and a tray of rice balls under a lid. Crews eat standing, masks pushed up on their foreheads. A slate by the hatch says whose turn it is to bring the next tray, and the slate is never wrong for long.

name: Robot garage
text: Low racks of cleaning robots charging in rows, each the size of a footstool. They go through the depot's cabs every night and come back with their bins full of whatever Sorrel dropped: buttons, hairpins, rice. The crew empty the bins by hand and send anything worth keeping to lost property.

name: Converter hall
text: Racks of power converters for the guideway, where cabs braking on this deck hand their energy to cabs speeding up. The hall is warm, dry and lamp-lit. A board by the door shows power coming back against power going out, and at the evening peak the two lines nearly touch.

name: Ramp works
text: The curved ramps where cabs turn between a core's channels and the tubes are relined here a section at a time, at night, while traffic runs in the twin channel. A curve's worth of guideway lies on trestles, numbered in chalk, like a staircase taken apart for cleaning.

name: Felt store
text: Bolts of felt for cab cabins, in every colour Sorrel has liked for a century, stacked to the ceiling. Heliox rings, so a bare cab would sound like a bucket; felt keeps it a room. The oldest colours go to the menders, who always ask first.

name: Dark store
text: Hand lamps, water, blankets and printed instructions for a beam cut, enough for every crew on the deck. In the Dark the cabs crawl and run on ration, two trips a day, and this is where the crews would sit it out. Every year they drill, and somebody finds a blanket they'd forgotten.

name: Apprentice bay
text: A corner given to apprentices from the lift school, with a cabin on a bench and a box of seals to practise on. They work at half the speed and twice the noise of the fitters next door, who pretend not to listen and correct them through the wall.

name: Quiet room
text: A small room with felt on every wall and six old chairs, for crews between shifts. Nobody lives on a line deck, but plenty of people close their eyes here for twenty minutes. The rule on the door is four words long: masks off, voices down.

name: Spare floor
text: Floor kept clear for whatever the Lattice needs next: another loop, a freight shaft, a bigger depot. For now it is bare and lamp-lit, with a spinball line painted down the middle by the crews of Ring {ring}, who play at break. Their scores are chalked on the wall going back eleven years.

name: Pump room
text: Pumps that top up the tubes with helium and hold each one at the deck's own pressure, so the berth seals have nothing to push against. The room hums one low, steady note. The crew claim they can tell from the pitch which tube is thirsty, and nobody has proved them wrong.

name: Platoon yard
text: A closed loop of tube where rebuilt cabs run in strings, nose to tail, and brake together at a signal until every one holds its gap. Nobody rides. The crew watch on screens from a gallery and call a clean run a good string, which is the highest praise on the deck.

name: Crew berths
text: A row of four berths where the deck's crews call cabs, like any lobby but with no bench and a rule board in large letters: one party to a cab, masks off before boarding, hold on when it leans. Someone has added a fifth rule in chalk: say anti.
